==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Quibble&min=Quibble&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Verify.Quibble: Verify writes a relaxed variant of json by default, which Quibble cannot
        // parse, so strict json is required. This changes every snapshot in the project to real json.
        // It has to come first: Initialize() below throws without it, and it sets Initialized before
        // it throws, so a failed call cannot be retried.
        VerifierSettings.UseStrictJson();
        // Verify.Quibble: registers a string comparer for json, so a mismatch is reported per JSON
        // path rather than as a diff of the whole file.
        // Both calls run before InitializePlugins(), which would otherwise initialize Quibble first,
        // with strict json still off.
        VerifyQuibble.Initialize();

        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/QuibbleTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Quibble&min=Quibble&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
// Verify.Quibble: Reports a failing json snapshot as structural, JSON-path level differences instead of as a text diff.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Quibble
// Note: VerifierSettings.UseStrictJson() is mandatory and has to run first. Initialize() sets
// Initialized before it throws about strict json, so a failed call cannot be retried.
// Note: Strict json changes every snapshot in the project from Verify's relaxed format to real
// json, so it is not a drop in for an existing suite.
// Note: It registers a string comparer for json, so it takes precedence over Verify.DiffPlex for
// json snapshots. A per test UseDiffPlex() overrides it again.
// Note: An empty verified file is treated as {}.
// Note: Quibble is an F# library, so FSharp.Core arrives transitively.
// Note: There are no settings methods or per test toggles: the only configuration is the
// UseStrictJson() call.
public class QuibbleTests
{
    // With strict json on, the snapshot is a .verified.json rather than Verify's relaxed txt.
    // When a value changes, the failure reads: String value difference at $.Property1: ValueC
    // vs ValueA, instead of showing both files in full.
    [Fact]
    public Task Json()
    {
        var target = new
        {
            Property1 = "ValueA",
            Property2 = "ValueB"
        };
        return Verify(target);
    }
}
